intro: A cause can be expressed verbally — with a clause — or nominally — with a preposition and a noun — and fluent German switches between them. Verbal: weil / da (verb last), denn (verb second, coordinating), deshalb / daher / folglich (adverb, verb second). Nominal: wegen + Gen (because of, neutral), aufgrund + Gen (on the basis of, formal), dank + Gen/Dat (thanks to, positive), aus + Dat (out of — for a conscious motive: aus Angst, aus Neugier, aus Liebe), vor + Dat (from — for an involuntary reaction: vor Freude weinen, vor Kälte zittern, vor Angst schreien). Turning weil es regnete into wegen des Regens means finding the noun (Regen), choosing the preposition, and putting the noun in the genitive. Turning it back means finding the verb again. Written German — reports, academic text, newspaper articles — lives in the nominal versions; speech lives in weil. Being able to do both is the mark of an advanced speaker.
tips[0].title: Verbal: weil / da / denn / deshalb
tips[0].text: …, weil es regnete (verb last) · Da es regnete, … (verb last, often sentence-initial, formal) · …, denn es regnete (verb second) · Es regnete, deshalb blieben wir (adverb, verb second). Four grammars, one meaning.
tips[0].check.why: The verb kam comes straight after the gap, so you need an adverb that takes position 1: deshalb. After weil the verb goes last; after denn the subject comes first.
tips[1].title: Nominal: wegen / aufgrund / dank + Genitiv
tips[1].text: wegen des Regens (neutral) · aufgrund der hohen Kosten (formal, on the basis of) · dank ihrer Hilfe (positive cause). All three take the genitive in writing (dank also dative). The noun is usually the -ung / -heit / -keit form of the verb or adjective.
tips[1].trap: 'because of the rain' has no case; wegen des Regens does. And the noun must exist: weil es regnete → Regen; weil sie half → Hilfe; weil es teuer war → die hohen Kosten.
tips[1].check.why: aufgrund takes the genitive: masculine des, adjective -en, and the noun adds -s.
tips[2].title: aus (motive) vs vor (reaction)
tips[2].text: aus Angst / Neugier / Liebe / Mitleid / Höflichkeit — a reason you act on. vor Freude / Angst / Kälte / Schmerz / Aufregung — a state that overwhelms you (weinen, zittern, schreien). No article after either.
tips[2].check.why: Blushing is not a choice but a reaction that overwhelms you, so it is vor + feeling. aus is for a motive you act on.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].b: vor Freude, vor Angst, vor Kälte
tips[3].title: Find the noun, pick the preposition, add the genitive
tips[3].text: weil es stürmte → der Sturm → wegen → wegen des Sturms. weil du geholfen hast → die Hilfe → dank → dank deiner Hilfe. Three moves, every time.
tips[3].check.why: Find the noun (das Wetter), pick the preposition (aufgrund), add the genitive: des schlechten Wetters.
remember[0]: weil / da / denn / deshalb ↔ wegen / aufgrund / dank + Genitiv.
remember[1]: aus = motive (aus Angst), vor = reaction (vor Angst zittern).
mistakes[0].why: wegen takes a noun; weil takes a clause.
hook: Say 'because it rained' two ways, weil es regnete and wegen des Regens, and switch between spoken and written German at will.
